artifacts.purpose: Main presentation applying DIO to open-source projects as distributed, evolving identity-bearing objects across technical, community, governance, and machine-facing representations.

term_rationales.artificial intelligence: The presentation explicitly identifies AI systems and AI-generated descriptions or recommendations as machine-facing representations of open-source projects.
term_rationales.knowledge graphs: The presentation explicitly names knowledge graphs as one of the machine-readable surfaces through which an open-source project is represented.
term_rationales.open-source project identity: The presentation treats the open-source project itself, rather than only its repository, as the identity-bearing object.
term_rationales.distributed project identity: The page describes the project as distributed across code, packages, documentation, governance, contributors, community, and machine-facing surfaces.
term_rationales.project continuity across change: The central question asks what makes a project remain the same project when maintainers, repositories, package names, licenses, and governance change.
term_rationales.software project governance: Governance structures and their changes are explicitly listed as identity-relevant project surfaces.
term_rationales.distributed representational state: The project is described as one logical entity represented across heterogeneous technical, human, and machine surfaces.
term_rationales.identity-preserving variation: The presentation distinguishes changes in maintainers, repositories, packages, and governance from the continuity of the project referent.
term_rationales.referential continuity: The central identity-continuity question concerns whether changed representations still refer to the same open-source project.
term_rationales.semantic coherence: The page explicitly frames the problem as maintaining coherence across the project's distributed identity representations.
term_rationales.Identity Collapse: The presentation explicitly names identity collapse as a risk when the project's distributed representations are not kept coherent.
